title: Merci !
subtitle: Four ways to say thank you
register: informal with friends (tu), polite with strangers (vous)
review: Draft written by Claude. Check the text before recording audio.
intro: A present, a bakery, a dinner, a stranger in the street: four short scenes, and a different thank-you in each. Listen for who says tu and who says vous.

lines.text: Bon anniversaire, Emma ! Tiens, c'est pour toi.

tr.en: Happy birthday, Emma! Here, this is for you.

lines.text: Oh ! Un cadeau ? Qu'est-ce que c'est ?

tr.en: Oh! A present? What is it?
Open it!

lines.text: Une écharpe ! Elle est magnifique. Merci beaucoup !

tr.en: A scarf! It's gorgeous. Thanks a lot!

lines.text: De rien. Le bleu, c'est ta couleur.

tr.en: You're welcome. Blue is your colour.
I love it. Thank you, Lucas!
Hello! What would you like?

lines.text: Bonjour ! Une baguette et deux croissants, s'il vous plaît.

tr.en: Hello! A baguette and two croissants, please.
Here you are. Anything else?
That's all, thanks.
That's three euros fifty.
Here you go. Thank you, have a nice day!
Thank you! Goodbye!

lines.text: Il est tard. Je dois partir.

tr.en: It's late. I have to go.

lines.text: Déjà ? Tu veux un dernier café ?

tr.en: Already? Would you like one last coffee?

lines.text: Non merci, c'est gentil. Le dîner était délicieux !

tr.en: No thanks, that's kind of you. Dinner was delicious!

lines.note: était = was. The one verb in the past here: c'était délicieux is worth learning whole.

tr.en: Thank you! I'm glad.
Thanks for everything, Emma.
My pleasure. Get home safely!
Thanks again! Good night!

lines.text: Excusez-moi, monsieur. Je cherche la gare.

tr.en: Excuse me, sir. I'm looking for the station.

lines.text: La gare ? C'est tout droit, puis à gauche.

tr.en: The station? It's straight ahead, then left.

lines.text: Tout droit, puis à gauche. C'est loin ?

tr.en: Straight ahead, then left. Is it far?
No, five minutes on foot.
Thank you, sir.

lines.text: Je vous en prie. Bonne journée !

tr.en: You're welcome. Have a nice day!

notes: With friends: merci, merci beaucoup, and the answers de rien or avec plaisir.
With strangers: je vous remercie is more formal than merci. The polite answer is je vous en prie (with a friend: je t'en prie).
C'est tout, merci answers « Et avec ceci ? » in a shop: 'That's all, thanks.'
Merci à vous returns the thanks: 'No, thank YOU.'
Merci pour tout closes a visit or a long favour. Encore merci is for when you have already said thank you once.

questions.q: Lucas thanks a man he does not know. What does he say?
questions.why: Je vous remercie is the formal thank-you, for strangers and for people you say vous to.

questions.q: The baker asks « Et avec ceci ? ». Emma wants nothing more. What does she say?
A friend says « Merci beaucoup ! ». Which answer fits?
questions.why: De rien = 'You're welcome', between friends. More polite: je vous en prie.

questions.q: Lucas has already said thank you. At the door he says it once more. Which words does he use?
questions.why: Encore merci = 'Thanks again', a warm way to sign off.
